answer: An earned-history gate stops cheap aliases. A new agent starts with zero trust and must complete 12 small paid jobs over 14 days before it can bid on high-value work, and every completed job is written to the nebula ledger, a public record every peer can read. At each epoch summit, independent auditors compare their mirror copies of the ledger. An alias whose claimed jobs do not match the mirror is flagged at once. The flagged alias loses all accumulated trust and its pending pay is frozen for 30 days, so spinning up 100 fresh aliases costs weeks of real work and earns nothing.
